assets.description: The foundation: four debarked logs laid side by side over one building-grid square, resting on two cross beams with a leg under each end. Each deck log differs a little in thickness, length, and turn, and the logs and beams show darker cut ends. The legs reach down to the ground, so they grow longer on the low side of a slope. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction has one stage per log: each delivered log stays in its place and turns solid during its stage, while the legs and beams fade in during the first stage.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The log wall: a 2 m stack of debarked logs laid along one edge of a foundation square. Each delivered log is cut in two, so each build stage lays two courses. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction lays the courses from the bottom up: each delivered log's two courses stay in their places and turn solid during its stage. A finished wall between the camera and the player fades out.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The door frame: two debarked-log posts on one edge of a foundation square, with a lintel across the top, 2 m tall. The doorway stays open. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction puts up the left post, the right post, then the lintel: each stays in its place and turns solid during its stage. A finished frame between the camera and the player fades out.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The roof frame: the timber skeleton of one foundation square, between the walls and the roof. Hewn beams, debarked logs squared with an adze, with chamfered corners, shallow adze marks, and pale cut ends, lie level on the top of every wall and door frame on the square's edges. Their square shape sets them apart from the round wall logs. The beams on the lower walls, which run along z, are hewn taller, so every beam top is level. A beam reaches about 0.15 m past the walls where no frame carries on beyond its end, so it stays under the steep eaves. Three hewn rafters, a little narrower than they are tall, rest on the beams and slope 35 degrees the way the frame faces, so the planks lie flat on them. Where the front of a frame is an eave, the rafters reach on past the wall, under the roof's overhang. Where a slope rises above the beams, as at each end of a ridge, the high side of a shed roof, or the step beside a lower roof, plank gable ends (the gable-end draft) close the gap up to the roof. The frame's cost pays for them. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction has one stage per log: the beams along x, the beams along z, then the rafters one by one, with the gable ends going up with the last rafter. Each part stays in its place and turns solid during its stage. It hides with the roof above the player.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The cabin roof section: planks laid on the roof frame of one foundation square, the same planks the sawhorse cuts. It slopes 35 degrees the way its frame does, and sections one behind another share one continuous slope. Two rows that slope away from each other meet at a ridge, where the planks of the slope down to +z or +x reach a little past it, over the other slope. Grey, weathered planks lie in 6 overlapping rows across the slope, from the eaves up. Each row is short planks side by side, running down the slope, with ragged, staggered lower ends that are a little darker. Each plank lies a little less steep than the roof, so its lower end lifts over the row below and every row casts a clear shadow line. Where an edge has no section beside it, the planks reach 0.5 m past the outside of the wall, over the eaves, the gable ends, and the high side of a shed roof. As a blueprint it shows see-through, and construction lays one row of planks per stage. The roof above the player hides when they stand under it. Its valley pieces are the separate draft asset roof-corners, and its gable ends the draft asset gable-end.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The valley pieces of the cabin roof and its frame. No roof has a hip. Where a frame's downhill neighbour slopes at right angles to it, one wing ends against another, and the frame becomes a valley, where the two slopes meet in a gutter. At the corner of an L-shaped or U-shaped cabin, the corner frames' own turns decide which wing runs through: the wing that slopes the same way as them. The player changes this by turning the corner frames with R. Where the butted wing is deeper, its slope starts higher and runs over the corner square as a straight section, and its ridge stands above the through-roof's. The frame has a debarked-log rafter along each low edge and one corner to corner under the line where the slopes meet. Six rows of weathered planks, made like the straight section's, are laid on both slopes from the eaves up, each cut along the meeting line and reaching a little past it, so each slope tucks under the other. Construction stages match the straight frame's and roof's.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The plank gable ends of the cabin roof. They close the gap between what is under an edge of a roof section and its planks: the triangle between the wall top and the roof at each end of a ridge or a shed roof, and the step where a taller wing's roof stands above a lower one. Each is a row of upright sawn planks, grey and weathered like the roof's, side by side along the edge with a thin gap between them. Each plank stands on the frame's beam or the lower roof and is cut at its top to the slope above, so the gable end meets the roof with no gap. They appear on their own, and go up with the last rafter of the roof frame, whose cost pays for them. The player never builds one alone.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

It is built in stages: each stick, then each strip of bark, fades in and is lowered into place.

assets.description: The player debarking a log on the ground with a drawknife: the player stands just off the nearer end of the log, facing along it. A person stripping bark bends over the log with knees bent and hips back, holds the drawknife by both handles, sets the blade into the bark at the far side, and pulls it back towards the knees, rocking back with the hips. Then they lift the blade clear and reach out for the next stroke. The feet stay planted and the axe goes on the back. It is posed in code over the idle clip, and reads apart from the chop's side swing, the split's overhead drop, and the build's squat and press.
assets.source: Built in code in this project
approvalNotes: 2026-11-12: The owner approved standing the player just off the nearer end of the log, so each stroke runs along it.

assets.description: The player going to sleep on a laid bedroll and waking. A person going to bed on a mat steps onto it, sits, and lies back with the head at the rolled blanket, then lies still. The view dims to black while the night passes, and lights up on the morning. Then the person sits up, gets their feet under them, and stands. The body plays KayKit's Lie_Down, Lie_Idle, and Lie_StandUp clips, a little faster than made; code times the step onto the bedroll, the dimming, and the sky change. Game logic waits while it plays. It reads apart from the build's squat: the whole body goes down flat.
assets.source: KayKit Character Pack: Adventurers 1.0 by Kay Lousberg, https://kaylousberg.itch.io/kaykit-adventurers (also https://github.com/KayKit-Game-Assets/KayKit-Character-Pack-Adventures-1.0). Characters/gltf/Barbarian.glb, unchanged. Clips Lie_Down, Lie_Idle, and Lie_StandUp

The feet stay planted and the axe goes on the back. It is posed in code over the idle clip, and reads apart from the chop's side swing and the split's overhead drop.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The HUD: woodland panels of dark bark with warm text and line icons, in the hotbar and wheel layout. The backpack is a hotbar at the bottom centre, with its weight. The build and craft buttons sit at the right end of the hotbar, apart from the backpack contents. They are larger buttons, stacked one above the other so the hotbar stays one row high. Each shows an icon, a name, and its key: "Build B" and "Craft C". Need bars sit above the hotbar, each with its name beside its icon. A low need pulses. The panels and open chest sit above them. While placing, the hint names its keys, such as "R to rotate · Esc to cancel". The clock is top left and the pause button top right. Build and craft open as lists above their buttons. A build row shows the structure's icon, name, and cost. A craft row shows the result's icon, the recipe name, its cost and time, and what it lacks.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The chest: a rough box hewn from debarked logs, 0.9 m wide and 0.55 m deep. Its body has a square post at each corner, three stacked planks in each wall with thin gaps between them, and a wooden grip on each end. Its lid is three planks laid side by side with a small overhang, held by two battens across the top. Each plank is a slightly different shade, and cut ends show pale. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction builds the body in the first stage and puts on the lid in the second.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The sawhorse: a beam of debarked log, 1.2 m long, resting 0.75 m up in the crook of two pairs of crossed legs, one pair near each end. The legs spread 0.6 m at the foot. Every part is painted like the debarked log, with drawknife streaks, bark scraps near the ends, knots, and darker heartwood on the cut ends. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction stands up the legs in the first stage and lays the beam in the second.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The sled: two log runners made from the logs asset's Kenney log, stretched to 1.8 m and lying side by side 0.8 m apart, with four crooked sticks laid across them. The front of each runner curves up and narrows like a skid. Dark rope lashes each stick to each runner in an X, and a tow rope runs in a V from the runner tips to a loop in front. The runners show dark bark and pale cut ends, and the sticks are the stick colour with pale cut ends. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its runner's place, and construction lays one runner per log, then one lashed cross piece per stick; the last brings the tow rope. A finished sled shows the 0 to 6 logs and debarked logs on it, lying along the runners: logs first, then debarked logs, stacked in a pyramid of three on the cross pieces, two above, and one on top. They use the logs and debarked-log shapes. A sled the player has dragged points the way it was last pulled, front first, at any angle.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: Icons drawn in the build icons' shaded style: the sled, seen from the front left and a little above, with two log runners whose front tips curl up like skids, the far runner darker and higher up, four crooked sticks lashed across them with dark rope Xs, and a pale tow rope running in a V from the tips to a loop in front. It shows on the sled's build menu tile and on the hotbar's sled cell while the player drags a sled. The log, a log on its side with dark bark and a pale cut end, shows in the sled's cost.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: A woodpile: two rails of debarked log on the ground, held in by two stakes at each end, with logs, debarked logs, and firewood stacked across them, four to a layer, from empty to full at five layers. Logs, debarked logs, and firewood use their approved shapes. Each layer rests in the gaps of the one below. As a blueprint, the rails and stakes show see-through.
assets.source: Built in code in this project
approvalNotes: 2026-11-11: The owner approved the stacked version: approved log, debarked log, and firewood shapes, layers nested in the gaps, debarked rails, and four stakes.

assets.description: How each kind of dropped thing looks on the ground, from one to many. A pile shows one copy of its kind for each thing it holds, up to 12. Firewood lies in a stack of 5, 4, then 3, each layer resting in the gaps of the one below. Bark lies in up to three rows of strips, each strip nested in the one below. Tools, food, the pot, and the bedroll spread around the middle. Firewood, bark, mushrooms, and the pot reuse their approved shapes. The axe has a steel head and a handle painted red at its end, the knife a bright blade, the drawknife a blue-steel blade with two wooden handles, and the steel and flint is the "steel-and-flint" asset. A handful of berries is seven red berries on a leaf. Dropped sticks never form a pile: they lie as normal sticks. The saw blade, the saw, and the plank are rough draft shapes added by the crafting feature.
assets.source: Built in code in this project
approvalNotes: 2026-11-11: The owner approved keeping rough draft shapes for the saw blade, the saw, and the plank in the pile until they are polished.

Its backpack icon shows the C-steel, the flint above it, and orange sparks flying off the flint.
